title: Without a memo the same subproblem is solved again on every branch; with one, a repeat is a lookup
caption: The call tree of paths(2, 3), drawn three levels deep. Each node is a call paths(r, c); row 0 and column 0 are base cases (1 path).

frames.text: paths(2, 3) = paths(1, 3) + paths(2, 2): the cell above plus the cell on the left. Each of those calls splits the same way.
Already at depth 2, paths(1, 2) is computed on both branches, and paths(1, 1) three times. Every repeat redoes its whole subtree, so the work multiplies at every level: exponential.
With a memo the first paths(1, 2) is computed and stored. The second one is a dictionary lookup, and its subtree is never expanded. The same goes for the second paths(1, 1).
Each distinct (r, c) is now computed once: time = number of states × work per state = O(rows · cols).
